blockdesc-generatorconsole-*: Place it facing the spot where the generator should stand: the tower rises eight blocks behind it, over a shaft sunk deep into the rock. Deliver materials here: each stage goes up piece by piece as its materials arrive. Breaking the console abandons the project.
blockdesc-steampipe-*: Carries steam from a generator's steam ports. Pipes join end to end; use a pipe fitting to turn a corner or branch. A pipe that is carrying steam warms anyone close to it.
blockdesc-pipejunction: Joins steam pipes on every side: for corners, tees and crossings.
blockdesc-steammain-*: A two-block-wide steam line for the generator's large ports. Set one against the mouth of a port or the end of another main and it lines up with it. Ordinary steam pipes can tap a main anywhere along it.
blockdesc-mainjunction: Joins steam mains on every side: for corners, tees and crossings.
blockdesc-distributor-straight-*: Splits a steam main into four small pipes. The main goes in one end; four outlets, one to each block of the far end, take pipes or pipe runs. Set it against the end of a main or a fitting and its inlet lines up.
blockdesc-distributor-drop-*: Splits a steam main into four small pipes that leave underneath, so they can go down and away. The main goes in one side; the four outlets on its underside take pipes or pipe runs.
blockdesc-wallpass-*: A solid block of wall with a pipe mount on each of two opposite sides, so a pipe can go through a wall without leaving a gap. Set it in the wall while looking through it: one mount faces you, the other faces away. Each mount takes a pipe laid against it or one pipe run.
blockdesc-radiator-*: A cast-iron column radiator, two blocks long. Its two hookups are on its back, one behind each block, at a right angle to its length, so it stands along the wall its pipe comes through. Each takes a pipe or a pipe run; a pipe can also feed it from underneath. Set it against a wall and it backs onto it. With steam in it, it gives five times the warmth of a pipe.
blockdesc-floorgrate: A floor block to walk on, with a heating coil under the grating. Feed it with a pipe or a pipe run to the mount underneath, or a pipe against any side. Grates laid side by side pass steam along, so one feed warms a whole floor. With steam in it, it gives three times the warmth of a pipe.
blockdesc-tentstove-*: A small pot-bellied stove for a tent or a hut. Put fuel in by hand, then light it as you would a firepit. It needs a flue standing on it that reaches open sky; the flue can go up through tent cloth. Fuel lasts three times as long as in a firepit.
blockdesc-stoveflue-*: Flue for a tent stove. Stack lengths on the stove until the end is in the open; it can go through tent cloth or a wall and closes the hole it makes. An elbow turns a rising flue out sideways, an upturn turns a lying flue back up, and a cap on top keeps the rain out.
stove-noflue: It needs a flue standing on it.
stove-flueblocked: The end of the flue is under cover; it has to come out under open sky.
blockdesc-steamhub: A heater two blocks square and six high that hangs from a steam main. Set it under a main fitting or the end of a main coming down; it takes a main on top and nothing else. With steam in it, it warms the ground below for twelve blocks round, most strongly close by. A steam hub tower builds the whole thing.
blockdesc-hubstand: Set it on the ground and it raises a steam hub on a tower: a frame on four legs, four blocks square, that tapers in over its last four blocks to carry a main fitting, with the hub hanging inside on a main dropped from the fitting, three blocks above the ground. It lines the fitting up with a large port or the end of a steam main exactly as a main stand does; anywhere else the fitting stands 14 blocks up. It needs at least ten blocks of height.
blockdesc-steamvalve-*: A length of pipe with a valve in it. Each click opens it a step, each sneak-click closes it a step, from shut to fully open in eight. Part open it holds steam back: each step lets 5 more through. The pointer over the wheel lies along the pipe when it is open and across it when it is shut.
blockdesc-steamgauge-*: Put it in a line of pipe. It carries three small dials. Left: the steam that can reach it, with a green zone that starts at what everything further along the line draws and moves as you build, and red above for more than is needed. Middle: what everything further along draws. Right: how well that draw is being met. Pipes join on three sides and underneath; the dials face you.
steam-short: Starved: getting {0}% of the steam it draws.
blockdesc-catwalk-*: A metre of catwalk with a handrail each side, for the block above a pipe. It stands on legs that reach the ground either side of the pipe. Put a flight of crossover steps at each end.
blockdesc-catwalkstair-*: A flight of steps one block high, with handrails, up to a crossover catwalk. Set it down facing the way you want to climb.
blockdesc-borer: Raises coal onto a pile beside it for as long as it has steam; bring a pipe to any side. It raises a fixed amount an hour, and more for coal in the rock within 12 blocks around and 32 below. That is counted once, when it is set down, and kept: mining the seam afterwards costs nothing, and it never runs out.
blockdesc-bucketconveyor-*: Carries coal from coal piles to the generator's console. Any conveyors that touch are one line; it draws from the top of every pile the line touches.
heap-count: {0} coal in this block of the pile.
borer-survey: Found {0} blocks of coal in the rock when it was set down.
borer-rate: Raising {0} coal an hour (up to {1} with all the steam it draws).
borer-blocked: No room beside it for its coal pile.
console-burn: Burning {0} an hour to send out {1} steam: about {2} hours left.
console-coaled: {0} coal into the bunker: it holds {1}.
console-nocoal: There is no coal in the bunker. Put coal in with coal in hand, or bring it by bucket conveyor.
wreck-hull: A section of the ship's hull
blockdesc-shipplate: Riveted iron plate from the wrecked freighter. Broken out, it gives iron bits to smelt.
blockdesc-shipcrate: Cargo from the freighter's hold. Break it open: iron, nails, rope, coal, and now and then a tool.
itemdesc-boilersection: A slab of plate cut from a ship's boiler. Too heavy to stack. On its own in the crafting grid it is cut up into three iron plates.
blockdesc-panel-*: Part of the building kit. A wall panel stands a quarter of a block thick on one edge of a cell, the edge nearest where you aim; a floor lies along the bottom and a ceiling along the top. One cell can hold a panel on every side, so corners need no special piece and rooms keep their full size. Break a panel to take just that one back.
blockdesc-roofslope-*: A block of roof at forty-five degrees. Set it down and its low edge faces you.
game:ingameerror-froststory-panel-taken: There is already a panel there
blockdesc-heatpipe-*: A low pipe that lies on the ground and joins whatever pipe, fitting or port is beside it, turning corners and branching by itself. Low enough to step over. Carrying steam, it gives off twice the warmth of an ordinary pipe.
blockdesc-tentrod-*: A pole one block long. Rods set end to end make uprights, ridges and ground rails for tent cloth to hang from.
blockdesc-tentcloth: With cloth in hand, click a tent rod, then another rod or the edge of any block: a panel is stretched between them, as wide as the whole pole. Hold the sprint key on the second click for a triangle, drawn to the nearest end of a pole or corner of a block. It stirs in the wind, keeps rain out and holds warmth in. The same two clicks take it down. One cloth covers a block of area.
tent-started: Cloth hangs from this pole. Click another rod or a block's edge to stretch it there (hold sprint for a triangle to the nearest end or corner), or this rod again to cancel.
tent-needrod: Tent cloth hangs from a tent rod: click one first.
tent-same: A panel needs two different edges.
tent-toofar: That is too far to stretch one panel.
tent-needcloth: That panel takes {0} cloth; hold that many.
run-started: Pipe run started here. Click another fitting or port to string it, or this one again to cancel.
run-removed: Pipe run taken down; {0} pipes returned.
run-notfitting: A pipe run goes between fittings and ports.
run-same: A pipe run needs two different ends.
run-needsbig: A steam main can only be strung between main fittings and large ports.
run-noside: One of those has no free side facing the other.
run-toolong: That is too far for one run. Put a fitting in between.
run-needpipes: That run takes {0} pipes; hold that many.
blockdesc-mainstand: Set it on the ground and it raises a post with a steam main fitting on top. In line with a large steam port or the end of a steam main (within 48 blocks along the compass), the fitting comes up at that pipe's height and lined up with it, whatever the ground does, so the main can be run out to it level. Anywhere else it stands 14 blocks up.
blockdesc-mainpost: A lattice post, two blocks square, that carries a steam main fitting.
game:ingameerror-froststory-stand-height: A stand cannot be that tall, or there is no room above
steam-pipe-cold: Cold: not joined to a live steam port
stagedesc-shaft: A lined shaft sunk into warm rock under a headframe, with a foundation collar at its mouth. Everything above will stand on it, and everything the generator draws will come up through it.
stagedesc-valves: The main riser and its heavy gate valves. They bleed surges from the deep off into relief ports, so the pressure stays inside what the machine can bear.
stagedesc-pumps: Four pump towers on a feed-water ring main. They drive surface water down the injection lines, to where the rock turns it into superheated steam.
stagedesc-core: The vessel where rising steam is split through the distribution header into working lines, for pumps, light, heat and industry. Eight steam ports come up through the pad rim for them.
stagedesc-frame-a: A riveted portal frame that takes the load of the upper works. The generator needs two, set crosswise.
stagedesc-frame-b: The second portal frame, set across the first. Together they carry the hull and the stack.
stagedesc-hull: An insulating steel shell around the core, with heat-exchange risers up its flanks, relief valves on the shoulder, two service galleries and four large steam ports over the first of them. It throws heat back inward and lets the operators decide how much of it escapes.
stagedesc-jacket: An outer shell of eight panels hung round the upper tower, clear of the galleries, on beams off the frames and the hull. It goes up in opposite pairs so the tower stays in balance, and keeps the cold off the crown.
step-corelower: Core plinth, lower vessel and steam ports
step-hulla: Hull, first lift with the doorways
step-hullb: Hull, second lift with the first gallery and the large ports
step-hullc: Hull, third lift with the second gallery
console-allcomplete: Generator: {0} complete. The generator is ready to be fired.
console-ready: The generator is complete and cold.
console-fired: The core catches. The generator is running.
console-banked: The core is banked. The generator goes cold.
console-tooshallow: This site is too close to the bottom of the world. The console needs to stand at height {0} or above.
itemdesc-furhood: A smoked-hide hood with a deep ruff of pale fur round the face and a drape over the shoulders. The ruff breaks the wind before it reaches the skin.
itemdesc-furparka: A heavy hide parka worn over a shirt, belted, with fur at the collar, the cuffs and the hem. The warmest and most windproof piece of an expedition outfit.
itemdesc-furtrousers: Thick wolf-grey fur trousers with hide knee patches. Bulky enough to slow the walk a little.
itemdesc-furmittens: Fur mittens with leather palms and a long cuff that goes over the sleeve. Fingers kept together stay warm longer.
itemdesc-furboots: Hide boots lined with fur, with hobnailed soles for the ice and a fur cuff at the top. Heavy on the feet.
itemdesc-snowgoggles: Iron cups with smoked glass on a leather strap. They keep the snow out of your eyes and cut the glare, so you can still find your way in a whiteout.
itemdesc-icepick-iron: A long spike on one side and an adze blade on the other. Breaks ice and packed snow quickly and makes a poor but usable weapon. Too soft for rock.
itemdesc-icesaw-iron: A long coarse-toothed blade on a T handle. Cuts lake ice, glacier ice and snow blocks out whole, so they drop as blocks to build with. Sawn lake ice leaves its water behind.
climate-storm-building: The wind is rising from the {0} and the horizon has gone white. A whiteout will be on you within {1} hours. Get under cover or near a fire.
climate-storm-hit: Whiteout. Wind from the {0}, snow you cannot see through. Stay in shelter or by heat.
climate-storm-severe: A killing whiteout is blowing in from the {0}. Anyone caught in the open will freeze. Get inside now.
climate-storm-easing: The storm is easing. The wind from the {0} is dropping.
climate-storm-over: The storm has blown itself out. The air is still and very cold.
climate-hypothermia: You are hypothermic: your hands are numb and your legs will not answer. Get out of the wind and next to heat.
climate-warmedup: Feeling comes back into your hands. You are warm enough to move properly again.
